chunks: ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) about the statement of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله): “Whoever dies while he has no Imam, then his death is a death of Jāhiliyyah.”
He said. I said, “A death of kufr?” He said, “A death of misguidance.”
I said, “So whoever dies today while he has no Imam, then his death is a death of Jāhiliyyah?” So he said, “Yes.”

key_terms.إِمَامٌ: the divinely designated leader whose recognition is necessary for guidance
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, whose statement is being explained
key_terms.ضَلَالٍ: misguidance or straying from the right path
key_terms.مِيتَةُ جَاهِلِيَّةٍ: a death resembling the state of pre-Islamic ignorance

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith ‘whoever dies without an Imam dies a death of Jāhiliyyah’ mean?
ai.summary: This hadith states that dying without recognizing an Imam is described as dying a death of Jāhiliyyah. Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) clarifies that this means a death of misguidance rather than kufr, affirming the centrality of the Imam in guidance.
